extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in science communication, bibliometrics, and computational social science
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and evaluating models that predict whether a research article will receive online press coverage, using features that quantify the article's attention on various online platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness as likelihood of receiving online press coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: There has been tremendous growth in the amount of scientific literature being published every year. Yet, very little of it receives press coverage. Mentions by news outlets often establish the relevance the research has to society in general. In the present study, we focused on better understanding the factors that contribute to a research article's newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper operationalizes 'newsworthiness' as the probability/likelihood that a research article will receive online press coverage and centers the analysis on factors that contribute to that outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use features quantifying attention on various online platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: We have built three classifiers to predict the likelihood of research article receiving online press coverage, based on features that quantify the attention it has received on various online platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features are altmetric-style measures (attention on online platforms). These attention metrics are treated as predictors of news coverage; the paper's methodology is to extract such features and feed them to classifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentions by news outlets as proxy for societal relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentions by news outlets often establish the relevance the research has to society in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors treat news mentions not just as an outcome variable but conceptually as an indicator of societal relevance, implying that coverage itself signals broader impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model evaluation using classifier accuracy (Random Forest accuracy = 0.92)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Random Forest classifier performed best with an accuracy rate of 0.92.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study evaluates predictive success using classification accuracy and compares multiple classifiers (three models). High accuracy for Random Forest is presented as evidence of the predictive value of the chosen features.
